requirements.heading: Reporting Policy
requirements.text: o "v": This document defines version 1 of TLSRPT, for which this value MUST be equal to "TLSRPTv1".

requirements.heading: Reporting Policy
requirements.text: Report submitters MAY ignore certificate validation errors when submitting reports via HTTPS POST.

requirements.heading: Reporting Policy
requirements.text: When sending failure reports via SMTP, Sending MTAs MUST deliver reports despite any TLS- related failures and SHOULD NOT include this SMTP session in the next report.

requirements.heading: Reporting Policy
requirements.text: Reports sent via SMTP MUST contain a valid DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) [RFC6376] signature by the reporting domain.

requirements.heading: Reporting Policy
requirements.text: Reports lacking such a signature MUST be ignored by the recipient.

requirements.heading: Reporting Policy
requirements.text: DKIM signatures MUST NOT use the "l=" attribute to limit the body length used in the signature.

requirements.heading: Reporting Policy
requirements.text: The DKIM TXT record SHOULD contain the appropriate service type declaration, "s=tlsrpt".

requirements.heading: Reporting Policy
requirements.text: If not present, the receiving system MAY ignore reports lacking that service type.

requirements.heading: Reporting Policy
requirements.text: tlsrpt-uri = URI ; "URI" is imported from [RFC3986]; ; commas (ASCII 0x2C), exclamation ; points (ASCII 0x21), and semicolons ; (ASCII 0x3B) MUST be encoded

requirements.heading: Reporting Policy
requirements.text: If the number of resulting records is not one, senders MUST assume the recipient domain does not implement TLSRPT.

requirements.heading: Reporting Policy
requirements.text: If the resulting TXT record contains multiple strings (as described in Section 3.3 of [RFC7208]), then the record MUST be treated as if those strings are concatenated without adding spaces.

requirements.heading: Reporting Policy
requirements.text: The record supports the ability to declare more than one rua, and if there exists more than one, the reporter MAY attempt to deliver to each of the supported rua destinations.

requirements.heading: Reporting Policy
requirements.text: A receiver MAY opt to only attempt delivery to one of the endpoints; however, the report SHOULD NOT be considered successfully delivered until one of the endpoints accepts delivery of the report.

requirements.heading: Reporting Policy
requirements.text: Parsers MUST accept TXT records that are syntactically valid (i.e., valid key/value pairs separated by semicolons) and implement a superset of this specification, in which case unknown fields SHALL be ignored.

requirements.heading: Reporting Schema
requirements.text: Because of this, even in the case where only a single policy was applied, the "policies" field of the report body MUST be an array and not a singular value.

requirements.heading: Report Time Frame
requirements.text: The report SHOULD cover a full day, from 00:00-24:00 UTC.

requirements.heading: Negotiation Failures
requirements.text: o "certificate-not-trusted": This is a label that covers multiple certificate-related failures that include, but are not limited to, errors such as untrusted/unknown certification authorities (CAs), certificate name constraints, certificate chain errors, etc. When using this declaration, the reporting MTA SHOULD utilize the "failure-reason-code" to provide more information to the receiving entity.

requirements.heading: Negotiation Failures
requirements.text: When using this declaration, the reporting MTA SHOULD utilize the "failure-reason- code" to provide more information to the receiving entity.

requirements.heading: General Failures
requirements.text: When a negotiation failure cannot be categorized into one of the "Negotiation Failures" stated above, the reporter SHOULD use the "validation-failure" category.

requirements.heading: General Failures
requirements.text: When this category is used, the reporter SHOULD also use "failure-reason-code" to give some feedback to the receiving entity.

requirements.heading: JSON Report Schema
requirements.text: In the case of Internationalized Domain Names [RFC5891], the domain MUST consist of the Punycode-encoded A-labels [RFC3492] and not the U-labels.

requirements.text: The filename is RECOMMENDED to be constructed using the following ABNF:

requirements.text: policy-domain = domain ; In the case of Internationalized Domain ; Names [RFC5891], the domain MUST consist of ; the Punycode-encoded A-labels [RFC3492] and ; not the U-labels.

requirements.heading: Report Filename
requirements.text: The extension MUST be "json" for a plain JSON file or "json.gz" for a JSON file compressed using gzip.

requirements.heading: Compression
requirements.text: The report SHOULD be subjected to gzip [RFC1952] compression for both email and HTTPS transport.

requirements.heading: Email Transport
requirements.text: The report MAY be delivered by email.

requirements.heading: Email Transport
requirements.text: The "TLS-Report-Submitter" value MUST match the value found in the domain [RFC5321] of the "contact-info" from the report body.

requirements.text: These additional headers SHOULD be included in the DKIM [RFC6376] signature for the message.

requirements.heading: Example Report
requirements.text: Note that, when sending failure reports via SMTP, Sending MTAs MUST NOT honor MTA-STS or DANE TLSA failures.

requirements.heading: HTTPS Transport
requirements.text: The report MAY be delivered by POST to HTTPS.

requirements.heading: HTTPS Transport
requirements.text: If compressed, the report SHOULD use the media type "application/tlsrpt+gzip"; otherwise it SHOULD use the media type "application/tlsrpt+json" (see Section 6, "IANA Considerations").

requirements.heading: HTTPS Transport
requirements.text: The receiving system MUST return a "successful" response from its HTTPS server, typically a 200 or 201 HTTP code [RFC7231].

requirements.heading: HTTPS Transport
requirements.text: The receiving system is not expected to process reports at receipt time and MAY store them for processing at a later time.

requirements.heading: Delivery Retry
requirements.text: In the event of a delivery failure, regardless of the delivery method, a sender SHOULD attempt redelivery for up to 24 hours after the initial attempt.

requirements.heading: Delivery Retry
requirements.text: If multiple retries are attempted, ideally they SHOULD be done with exponential backoff.

requirements.heading: Metadata Variances
requirements.text: If any of the items declared via subject or filename disagree with the report, the report MUST be considered the authoritative source.

requirements.heading: Report Type
requirements.text: The suffix "+gzip" MAY be used with any media type whose representation follows that established for "application/gzip".

requirements.heading: Report Type
requirements.text: Fragment identifier considerations: The syntax and semantics of fragment identifiers specified for +gzip SHOULD be as specified for "application/gzip".
